content:
Earlier this year, Apple closed part of the Apple Park visitor center, saying it was to "improve our store."

The space has now reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed the in-house augmented reality experience, powered by iPads, that allowed visitors to take a virtual tour of Apple Park.

When the Apple Park visitor center opened to the public in 2017, the company described the AR experience as follows:

Augmented reality brings a 3D model of the campus to life, inviting visitors to explore Apple Park in an immersive, engaging way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building, as well as tour one of the largest onsite solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the roof of the entire building and glimpse the layout of the interior collaboration spaces.

Before this renovation, the Apple Park visitor center was divided into three zones: the AR exhibit area, a traditionally designed Apple Store, and a café.

Apple has now eliminated the AR exhibit area and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. As MacRumors found, the refurbishment includes Avenues accessory display walls placed along the walls, as well as redesigned product display tables for showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park visitor center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac Commentary

The AR experience at the Apple Park visitor center was indeed one of a kind, but nine years on, I'm starting to feel that the space could be put to better use.

I hope Apple doesn't just turn it into another conventional retail store, but tries something else; fortunately the café is still there as a distinctive element of the Apple Park visitor center.
